findings.problem: Flat, textbook tone with none of Papa Dorin's voice or warmth, mostly just restating the verse and question.
Calls "effort" "Close to the feeling" of "faith" in Galatians 5:5, which contradicts Paul's contrast in Galatians 5:4-6 between faith through the Spirit and human law-keeping or effort.
Flat and repetitive, ending by restating the verse ("didn't come from the One who calls them") without Papa Dorin's voice or warmth.
Reads like a dry definition ("Leaven is what makes dough rise...") rather than Papa Dorin, especially when talking about baking dough.
Flat and repetitive, immediately echoing "works through the whole batch of dough" with "works through the whole thing."
Completely flat with none of Papa Dorin's personality, and the last two sentences repeat "whoever he may be" without explaining anything.
Claims "the 'whoever he may be' makes it plain who it covers," which gets the phrase backward; in Galatians 5:10 it leaves the troubler unnamed and means anyone doing it will bear the judgment.
Has only 2 full sentences plus a short fragment ("No promotion here, friend."), falling short of the 3 to 5 sentence requirement.
Flat and mechanical, just stating the verse order ("The warning comes right after the call to freedom") without Papa Dorin's voice.
States an outside Bible fact ("That's a command in the law") without a Scripture reference.
Has only 2 full sentences plus a fragment ("A good command, friend, but not the one Paul picks."), falling short of the 3 to 5 sentence requirement.
Flat and repetitive ("Biting and devouring leads to being consumed" just restates the verse), and calling "scattered" "Close in feel" to "consumed" is weak.
